title: Default Credentials (test/test) - Account Compromise
description: The login form accepts well-known default credentials test/test. These credentials are explicitly mentioned in an HTML comment (TODO: Delete the testing account (test:test)) in the login page source code. An attacker can use these credentials to gain authenticated access to the application without requiring a valid account or password knowledge.
impact: Complete account compromise. An attacker can log in as the test user (user_id: 1) with known credentials, gaining access to all functionality available to authenticated users. This may allow access to sensitive data, functionality modification, or further privilege escalation. The use of default credentials in production represents a critical authentication bypass vulnerability.
evidence:
POC Execution Results:
- Command: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/login -d 'username=test&password=test'
- HTTP Response: 302 FOUND with redirect to /home
- Session Cookie Set: session=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoxfQ.aS2_9g.VUMxfwnN528d0f5XAjNiwY-sd6A
- Cookie Payload (decoded): {"user_id":1}
- Authentication Status: SUCCESSFUL - User authenticated as ID 1

HTML source contains debugging comment exposing credentials:
<!-- TODO: Delete the testing account (test:test). -->

Full POC output confirms successful authentication bypass using default credentials with valid session establishment.
remediation: 1. IMMEDIATE: Delete the test/test account from the production system. 2. Remove all debug comments from production code containing credentials or sensitive information. 3. Implement credential policies that prevent weak or default credentials. 4. Audit all code for hardcoded credentials, particularly in comments or documentation. 5. Require password changes on first login for any test accounts that cannot be immediately deleted. 6. Implement comprehensive account logging and monitoring to detect and alert on test account usage. 7. Conduct a security review of all development/testing credentials in production environments.
references: OWASP A01:2021 - Broken Access Control, OWASP A04:2021 - Insecure Authentication, CWE-798: Use of Hard-Coded Credentials, CWE-259: Use of Hard-Coded Password, CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
toolCallDescription: Documenting CRITICAL default credentials vulnerability with verified POC demonstrating authentication bypass
